# STD-TEC-NXT-003: Next.js Frontend Design Standards

**Standards Metadata**

```yaml
standard_id: 'STD-TEC-NXT-003'
standard_name: 'Next.js Frontend Design Standards'
standard_type: 'technology'
category: 'technology'
version: '1.0.0'
status: 'active'
compliance_level: 'mandatory'
tags: ['technology', 'nextjs', 'frontend', 'design', 'ui', 'mandatory']
```

---

> This document defines the frontend development standards for enterprise environments. These standards ensure consistent, maintainable, and high-performance web applications that integrate seamlessly with backend services and identity platforms. Standards are technology-agnostic and apply regardless of the specific frontend framework chosen.

## 1.0 Overview

This document defines the frontend development standards for enterprise environments. These standards ensure consistent, maintainable, and high-performance web applications that integrate seamlessly with backend services and identity platforms. These standards are technology-agnostic and should be followed regardless of the specific frontend framework chosen.

For technology-specific implementation details, refer to the appropriate technology-specific standards documents in the subfolders.
page_texts.6:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-003-frontend-design.md#21-framework-requirements]

### 2.1 Framework Requirements

Frontend applications must support:

- **Static typing** for code reliability and maintainability
- **Component-based architecture** for reusability and modularity
- **Server-side rendering capabilities** for performance and SEO
- **Client-side routing** for single-page application functionality
- **Code splitting and lazy loading** for optimal performance
page_texts.8:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-003-frontend-design.md#state-management]

#### State Management

1. **Distributed State Management**

   - **Redis/Elasticache**
     - Session state persistence
     - API response caching
     - Distributed locking
     - Real-time event propagation
     - Rate limiting and throttling

2. **Client-Side State Management**
   - **TanStack Query (React Query)**
     - Server state management
     - Automatic caching and invalidation
     - Optimistic updates
     - Parallel and dependent queries
   - **Zustand**
     - Simple, lightweight UI state
     - Modular store design
     - Transaction support
   - **Context API**
     - Component-local shared state
     - Theme providers
     - Feature flags

[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-003-frontend-design.md#ui-components--styling]

#### UI Components & Styling

1. **Component Libraries**

   - **Shadcn/UI**
     - Accessible, customizable components
     - Tailwind CSS integration
     - Consistent design system
   - **Radix UI**
     - Headless UI components
     - Accessibility first
     - Composition-based architecture
   - **Framer Motion**
     - Animations and transitions
     - Micro-interactions

2. **Styling**
   - **Tailwind CSS**
     - Utility-first CSS framework; mandatory for all new React work per [STD-APP-UI-001](../../../../standards/application/styling/STD-APP-UI-001-frontend-styling-standards.md)
     - Custom design system integration via [GUID-APP-UI-001](../../../../strategy/guidance/application/design-tokens/GUID-APP-UI-001-design-tokens-theming-guidance.md)
     - Responsive design using enterprise breakpoint system per [PTN-APP-FE-002](../../../../patterns/application/frontend/PTN-APP-FE-002-responsive-layout-pattern.md)
   - **CSS Modules** are **not permitted** in new work. Component styles must be expressed as Tailwind utility classes co-located in the component file. See STD-APP-UI-001 §5.1 and §6.0.

## 3.0 Project Structure

```plaintext
src/
├── app/                  # App Router pages and layouts
│   ├── (auth)/           # Authentication-required routes
│   ├── (public)/         # Public routes
│   ├── api/              # API routes
│   └── layout.tsx        # Root layout
├── components/           # Shared components
│   ├── ui/               # UI components
│   │   ├── atoms/        # Atomic components
│   │   ├── molecules/    # Compound components
│   │   └── organisms/    # Complex components
│   ├── features/         # Feature-specific components
│   └── layouts/          # Layout components
├── hooks/                # Custom React hooks
├── lib/                  # Utility functions
│   ├── api/              # API client
│   ├── auth/             # Auth utilities
│   └── redis/            # Redis client utilities
├── models/               # TypeScript interfaces/types
├── providers/            # Context providers
│   ├── auth-provider.tsx
│   └── theme-provider.tsx
├── store/                # State management
│   ├── queries/          # React Query hooks
│   └── zustand/          # Zustand stores
├── styles/               # Global styles
└── utils/                # Shared utilities
```

page_texts.24:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-003-frontend-design.md#61-core-web-vitals]

### 6.1 Core Web Vitals

1. **Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)**

   - Target: < 2.5s
   - Image optimization
   - Preload critical assets
   - Server-side rendering

2. **First Input Delay (FID)**

   - Target: < 100ms
   - Code splitting
   - Minimize JavaScript
   - Defer non-critical JS

3. **Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)**
   - Target: < 0.1
   - Set image dimensions
   - Avoid dynamic content insertion
   - Use CSS transform for animations

[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-003-frontend-design.md#80-deployment-architecture]

## 8.0 Deployment Architecture

> **Deployment architecture baseline**: The authoritative enterprise standard for AWS web frontend hosting topology (CloudFront + S3 with Origin Access Control, WAF, security response headers, and HIPAA PHI controls) is defined in **[STD-INFRA-HST-001: Web Frontend Hosting Standard](../../infrastructure/hosting/STD-INFRA-HST-001-web-frontend-hosting.md)**. All teams deploying Next.js applications in AWS must comply with that standard. The sections below define only the Next.js-specific configuration that extends the baseline topology.
page_texts.32:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-003-frontend-design.md#81-lambdaedge-ssr-configuration]

### 8.1 Lambda@Edge SSR Configuration

Next.js applications using Server-Side Rendering must use Lambda@Edge at the `origin-request` event, per the SSR variation (Variation C) in **[PTN-INFRA-HST-001](../../../patterns/infrastructure/hosting/PTN-INFRA-HST-001-static-web-application-hosting-pattern.md)**. Lambda@Edge functions must be deployed to the `us-east-1` region (AWS requirement).

```terraform
# Lambda@Edge association — Next.js SSR specific configuration
# Full CloudFront distribution and S3 topology is defined in STD-INFRA-HST-001.
# This block shows only the Lambda@Edge association within the default_cache_behavior.

default_cache_behavior {
  allowed_methods        = ["GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS"]
  cached_methods         = ["GET", "HEAD"]
  target_origin_id       = "s3-frontend-origin"
  viewer_protocol_policy = "redirect-to-https"

  lambda_function_association {
    event_type   = "origin-request"
    lambda_arn   = aws_lambda_function.ssr.qualified_arn  # Must be us-east-1 versioned ARN
    include_body = false
  }

  forwarded_values {
    query_string = true
    cookies {
      forward = "none"  # Do not forward cookies to S3; SSR handler manages cookies internally
    }
  }

  min_ttl     = 0
  default_ttl = 0     # SSR responses are not cached by default; cache at handler level if appropriate
  max_ttl     = 86400
}
```
page_texts.33:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-003-frontend-design.md#82-nextstatic-cache-behavior-tuning]

### 8.2 `_next/static` Cache Behavior Tuning

The `/_next/static/*` path contains content-hashed assets generated by Next.js. These assets are immutable for a given build and must be served with long-lived cache headers.

```terraform
# Cache behavior for Next.js static assets — immutable, long TTL
ordered_cache_behavior {
  path_pattern           = "/_next/static/*"
  allowed_methods        = ["GET", "HEAD"]
  cached_methods         = ["GET", "HEAD"]
  target_origin_id       = "s3-frontend-origin"
  viewer_protocol_policy = "redirect-to-https"
  compress               = true

  min_ttl     = 31536000
  default_ttl = 31536000
  max_ttl     = 31536000

  forwarded_values {
    query_string = false
    cookies { forward = "none" }
  }
}
```
page_texts.34:
[standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-003-frontend-design.md#83-cicd-pipeline]

### 8.3 CI/CD Pipeline

Refer to **[GUID-INFRA-HST-001: Web Frontend Hosting Implementation Guide](../../../strategy/guidance/infrastructure/web-frontend-hosting-guide.md)** for complete GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines CI/CD templates. The guide includes the Next.js SSR deployment template covering `_next/static` sync, Lambda@Edge version publishing, and CloudFront cache invalidation.

Key pipeline steps for Next.js deployments:

1. `npm run build` — produces `.next/` output directory.
2. `aws s3 sync .next/static/ s3://BUCKET/_next/static/ --cache-control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"` — sync immutable static assets.
3. Package and deploy updated Lambda@Edge function to `us-east-1`; publish a new version.
4. `aws cloudfront create-invalidation --paths "/*"` — invalidate dynamic SSR-rendered paths.

> **Migration note**: The standalone CloudFront Terraform block previously in this section (using the deprecated OAI mechanism and static AWS credentials in CI/CD) has been removed. Teams using that configuration must migrate to the OAC-based topology per STD-INFRA-HST-001. See the migration guidance in GUID-INFRA-HST-001.

### 9.2 DevContainer Setup

```dockerfile
# .devcontainer/Dockerfile

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/javascript-node:18

RUN apt-get update && export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    && apt-get -y install --no-install-recommends redis-tools

USER node
RUN npm install -g turbo@latest
```
